summary: Validated the new live-polling endpoint GET /api/conversations/{id}/messages/since end-to-end. Backend pytest: 12/12 passed (4 cursor edge cases + 2 auth-gating + 2 parity + 1 regression + 1 multi-user live update + 1 ready_at $or branch + 1 missing-cursor variant). Frontend smoke test: ConversationPage loads existing thread, renders 9 message bubbles, polls /messages/since every ~3s (4 calls in 7.5s, all 200 OK), composer remains visible — live-polling effect does NOT break initial load or send flow.

issues: Pre-existing React hydration error: nested <a> inside <a> — `org-card-chat-{id}` <Link> is rendered INSIDE the outer `org-card-{id}` <Link> in AppHome.js (~lines 155-218). Causes console errors on every page load and a hydration mismatch. Unrelated to messages/since work but worth fixing — wrap the inner chat link as a sibling using stopPropagation, not a descendant.

action_items: Pre-existing (not introduced by this change): fix nested <a> hydration warning in AppHome.js org card chat shortcut.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L2822-2884 get_messages_since — correctly reuses load_conv_or_403 for auth (verified: outsider gets 403, unauthenticated gets 401). Empty cursor short-circuits to []. ISO parsing handles trailing Z and naked timestamps (fromisoformat + tzinfo backfill). Garbage cursor → 400 with clear detail string. $or branch on ready_at correctly surfaces patched media messages — confirmed via direct Mongo patch test. Feedback aggregation pipeline mirrors get_messages exactly; up_count/down_count/my_feedback all present. _id excluded via projection so no ObjectId leak.

Potential micro-concern (NOT blocking): to_list(500) cap on the /since query. If a tab is hidden for hours and >500 messages accumulated, the client will only see the first 500 by timestamp asc and the cursor will advance past the rest. For team chats that's extremely unlikely; leave as-is, but worth a comment.

ConversationPage.js L324-384 — uses a ref + dual useEffects to keep the 3s interval stable while latest-cursor updates. document.hidden gate is in place (saves battery + LLM cost). Merge logic deduplicates by id and re-sorts by timestamp — handles the in-place media patch case correctly (same id, fresher ready_at, replaces existing bubble). Inflight guard prevents overlapping polls if a request hangs. Clean implementation.

Cursor URL is sent un-encoded (`cursor=2026-05-05T14:33:04.219000`). Axios encodes the params but `:` survives as-is in many backends. Backend handles it fine (verified 200s in browser network trace) so no action needed.
Multi-user verified: user B (a second user invited into A's open team) sees A's just-posted message via /since with cursor=<previous-newest> within one poll cycle. The product win is real.
